title: Why You See Names Hidden in Other Words
hook: Why do you sometimes see names inside other words?

narration.text: Your brain is constantly trying to make sense of ambiguous patterns.
It can spot familiar shapes, like letters, even in complex arrangements.
This is a form of pareidolia, where you see meaningful images in random data.
Your brain connects the shapes it knows, forming a name you recognise.
You can test this right now with some fancy, decorative fonts.
It is a fun trick of perception that happens all around us.
Try it and tell me if it worked on you in the comments, and subscribe for more surprising insights into your mind.

description: Have you ever spotted a person's name cleverly hidden within another word? This curious phenomenon, known as word pareidolia, is a fascinating trick of your brain. It is always seeking patterns, even in unexpected places.
topic: Why you sometimes see a person's name written as part of another word, known as a 'visual pun' or 'word pareidolia'. You can test this right now with some complex fonts.
